This project treats provisional evidence as provisional, on purpose. This page
tracks what's solid, what's a lead, and what's actively disputed, so a claim's
confidence level is never more than one click from the claim itself.

## Resolved

### UCLA's ICPSR founding-member status

Confirmed against the actual 1962 document, not just a later recollection or
a university's own marketing page. Warren Miller's own August 1962 founding
memo lists "University of California at Los Angeles" among the institutions
participating "as of July 30, 1962." See `miller-1962-considerations.md`.
This does not resolve the exact headcount (see below) or Marvick's personal
role (see below).

## Open conflicts {#pre-1977-connective-tissue}

### The "8 founding members" headcount: not simply wrong, now genuinely unresolved

This looked settled, then got more complicated instead of less. Two
independent counts put the full initial ICPSR membership above 8: Erik
Austin's founding-years essay counts 22 institutions from membership
records, and Warren Miller's own August 1962 memo names 21 directly, dated
"as of July 30, 1962." Both include UCLA. Neither has an "8" anywhere.

But ICPSR's current director, Maggie Levenstein, independently used the
figure "8" during a UCLA visit, not obviously drawing on UCLA's own page. And
ICPSR's own institutional archive at the Bentley Historical Library holds a
folder titled "Committee of Eight, Correspondence and Minutes, 1962-1963,"
per its finding aid (`umich-bhl-9938-finding-aid.md`). A plausible
reconciliation: "8" refers to a specific founding committee, not the full
21/22-institution membership roster. Both numbers could be correct,
describing two different things. Not confirmed. Nobody has read that folder,
and nobody has asked Levenstein what she meant. Either would settle this
faster than more inference.

### Eve Fielder's SRC directorship: 1964 or 1976?

Three internal sources say the archive merged into the Survey Research Center in
1964 "under Eve Fielder." A Fielder obituary cited in the deep-research report
says she became SRC's first director in 1976, the same year SRC was reportedly
incorporated into ISSR. Not resolved. Needs a documentary check (SRC records,
UCLA Sociology/Political Science department histories, or an earlier obituary
detail) before either date gets used as fact in the narrative.

### 1977's institutional home: four accounts, four answers

- Both 2017 decks: the archive came under **ISSR**.
- The Dataverse About page: **Donald Treiman** designed the framework; no
  institutional home named.
- The book-chapter draft: the archive was created "as part of the **Survey
  Research Center**"; no ISSR mention.
- External evidence (UCLA's 1977–78 General Catalog, per the deep-research
  report): ISSR is the named parent, with SRC as a component under it.

The catalog evidence points toward ISSR being correct and the book chapter's
SRC-only framing being the error. That's an inference though, not a confirmed
correction. Verify against the catalog directly.

### Marvick's claimed ICPSR founding role

Separate question from the headcount above, and also not resolved, though
closer than it was. ICPSR's own first annual report names its
initial council members, and Marvick isn't among them. Neither Austin's
founding-years essay nor Miller's own 1962 memo mentions him, though Miller's
memo doesn't name any individual faculty member from any institution, since
the Consortium was explicitly built on "institutional rather than individual
participation," so that absence carries less weight than his absence from
the council-member list does. What changed: Eulau's 1999 memorial establishes
that Marvick and Miller were close personal friends and research
collaborators for a full decade before either the archive or ICPSR existed,
together at Michigan's Survey Research Center in the early 1950s. That's a
real, documented mechanism for "through his efforts" to be true informally,
even though no document yet says it directly. His formally documented ICPSR
role is governing-board service from 1964, rising to chair of the ICPR
Council in 1966-67 (per Eulau), all after founding. The Dataverse page's
"through [Marvick's] efforts, UCLA was one of the founding members" is now
plausible rather than simply unsupported, but still not confirmed by any
document found so far.

### Donald Treiman's relationship to ISSR

The Dataverse page credits him with designing the 1977 framework but doesn't
mention ISSR. The deep-research report notes his CV supports depositor and
intellectual involvement but not necessarily a formal ISSR title. Whether he
was an ISSR-affiliated director or a faculty collaborator outside ISSR's own
leadership structure is unresolved. His living status is also unconfirmed.

### Newsletters

No digitized ISSR/SSDA newsletter or annual-report run has been found in any
public index checked (UCLA General Catalog, eScholarship, Internet Archive,
HathiTrust, Google Books, UCLA Digital Library). This is a negative search
result. It means "not found here," not "doesn't exist." The physical-location
inquiry (UCLA University Archives, former staff) is the live lead for this,
checking the week of 2026-08-03.

Tim recalls the newsletters referred to the unit informally as "the Data
Archive," and that this usage spanned multiple formal institutional eras
(ISSR, the ISR rename, standalone SSDA). Not yet confirmed since the
newsletters themselves haven't been found. Worth watching for once they
turn up: it would mean the informal "Data Archive" self-identification
persisted underneath at least three formal name changes, which would be a
nice thread connecting the 2017 internal decks' own tagline ("providing
archive and data services since 1961") back through the whole ISSR era.

## How to read confidence notes on this site

Where a claim in the narrative chapters carries a confidence note, it follows
this rough scale:

- **Very high**: a primary document in hand (CV, MOU, obituary, catalog entry)
- **High**: a named, dated claim from a credible source, not yet cross-checked
- **Moderate**: plausible, sourced, but only one account exists
- **Disputed / unresolved**: multiple sources actively disagree

## What hasn't been touched yet

- Independent verification of either deep-research report's citations, one by one
- Marvick's own papers (correspondence, project records from roughly 1959 to
  1964): the likeliest source for his actual stated motivation for founding
  the archive in 1961, which no source found so far documents directly
- The APSA oral history project: Eulau's memoir mentions Marvick interviewed
  him for it in 1988. Worth checking whether that collection includes other
  interviews Marvick conducted, or covers Marvick himself
- ICPSR's own institutional records at the Bentley Historical Library (Michigan):
  a finding aid has been reviewed, not the actual boxes. Specific targets
  identified: Council meeting minutes for 1966–67 (Marvick's chair years), the
  "Committee of Eight" correspondence from 1962–63, and a folder titled
  "Formation of a Data Repository, 1962." See `umich-bhl-9938-finding-aid.md`
- The cheapest possible next step on the "8 founders" question: just ask
  Maggie Levenstein, ICPSR's current director, what she meant. She's a named,
  reachable, current source who used the figure directly
- UCLA University Archives records (this site's research has been entirely
  public-web so far)
- Oral history outreach to any of the people listed on the [People](people.qmd)
  page
